name: CDP and LLDP
author: Recurse
subject: networking
description: Discover neighbors with CDP and LLDP, read summary and detail output, troubleshoot with them and decide where to turn them off.

lesson.intro: CDP and LLDP answer "who is on the other end of this cable?" with a hostname, port, model and often an IP address, without logging in to the neighbor. Learn to configure both, read their output fluently and know where to turn them off.
objectives: Describe what CDP and LLDP discover and why only direct neighbors
Read CDP and LLDP neighbor output, telling local and remote interfaces apart
Enable and disable CDP and LLDP globally and per interface
Use CDP to verify cabling, find phones and APs, and spot mismatches
Compare CDP and LLDP defaults and decide where to disable them

sections.title: Who is on the other end of this cable?
sections.key: CDP and LLDP are Layer 2 protocols that tell a device about its directly connected neighbors, and they work without any IP address.
sections.body:
You are handed a closet of unlabeled cables and asked to draw the network. Instead of tracing cables, ask the switch what it hears: devices advertise themselves out every interface, and neighbors store what they hear.

The **Cisco Discovery Protocol (CDP)** is Cisco's own. The **Link Layer Discovery Protocol (LLDP)**, IEEE 802.1AB, is the vendor-neutral standard. Both run directly over Layer 2, so they work even when IP is broken or not configured yet.

[[visual]]

Advertisements go to a multicast MAC (CDP `0100.0CCC.CCCC`, LLDP `0180.C200.000E`) that the receiver processes and **never forwards**. So each device learns only its direct neighbors.

[[visual 2]]

Discovery protocols build no forwarding table. They inform you, and help phones learn their voice VLAN.

visual.title: What a CDP neighbor tells you
rows: The neighbor's interface on this link
Router, switch, phone and so on

marks.text: Hears SW2 only: R1 is two hops away

sections.pitfall: Expecting CDP to map the whole network from one device. It shows only direct neighbors; to go further, log in to a neighbor using the IP address CDP gave you and look again.

check.question: R1 connects to SW2, and SW2 connects to SW1. CDP is enabled everywhere. Which neighbors does show cdp neighbors on SW1 list?
choices: SW2 and R1
SW2 only
R1 only
None, because CDP needs IP addresses
check.explanation: CDP messages are processed by the receiving device and never forwarded, so SW1 hears only its direct neighbor SW2. CDP runs at Layer 2 and works without any IP configuration.

sections.title: Reading show cdp neighbors
sections.key: In show cdp neighbors, Local Intrfce is your own port and Port ID is the neighbor's port; Device ID is the neighbor's hostname.
sections.body:
`show cdp neighbors` prints one line per neighbor. Its two interface columns are the exam's favorite trap.

[[code]]

[[visual]]

Read each line as "my port, your port". From SW2: its Gi1/0/21 goes to SW1's Gi1/0/24, and its Gi1/0/2 goes to R1's Gi0/0/1.

[[visual 2]]

`show cdp neighbors gi1/0/2` limits the output to one interface, handy on a 48-port switch full of phones and APs.

visual.title: The columns
rows: The neighbor's name, normally its hostname
**Your** interface, on the device where you typed the command
Seconds left before the entry is removed; jumps back up with each advertisement
R router, S switch, I IGMP, P phone, H host, M two-port MAC relay. CDP lists everything the neighbor supports, so a router often shows R S I

sections.code:
SW2# show cdp neighbors
Capability Codes: R - Router, T - Trans Bridge, B - Source Route Bridge
                  S - Switch, H - Host, I - IGMP, r - Repeater, P - Phone,
                  D - Remote, C - CVTA, M - Two-port Mac Relay

Device ID        Local Intrfce     Holdtme    Capability  Platform  Port ID
SW1              Gig 1/0/21        155             S I    WS-C2960X Gig 1/0/24
R1               Gig 1/0/2         131           R S I    C1111-8P  Gig 0/0/1

Total cdp entries displayed : 2
sections.pitfall: Swapping the columns. On SW2, "SW1  Gig 1/0/21 ... Gig 1/0/24" means SW2's own Gi1/0/21 connects to SW1's Gi1/0/24, not the other way round.

check.question: On SW2, a line reads: R1  Gig 1/0/2  131  R S I  C1111-8P  Gig 0/0/1. Which interface on R1 connects to SW2?
choices: GigabitEthernet1/0/2
Both, because CDP shows a shared link name
GigabitEthernet0/0/1
It appears only in show cdp neighbors detail
check.explanation: Port ID is the neighbor's interface, so R1 uses Gi0/0/1. Gi1/0/2 under Local Intrfce is SW2's own port.

sections.title: Going deeper: neighbors detail and show cdp entry
sections.key: show cdp neighbors detail, or show cdp entry NAME for one neighbor, adds the neighbor's IP address, full IOS version, native VLAN, duplex and VTP domain.
sections.body:
The summary says who is connected where. The detail view says how to reach the neighbor and what it runs.

[[visual]]

[[code]]

`show cdp entry SW1` prints the same block for one neighbor (the name is case sensitive; `show cdp entry *` shows all). A neighbor with no IP address yet still appears, with an empty address list.

That address turns CDP into a mapping tool:

[[visual 2]]

visual.title: What detail adds
rows: The neighbor's IP address: the main reason to use detail
The full model name, and capabilities in words
Your port and the neighbor's port, spelled out
VTP Management Domain, Native VLAN, Duplex
CDP version 2 extras for comparing settings across the link

visual.title: Map a network you cannot see

steps.label: `show cdp neighbors`
steps.detail: Note each neighbor and both interfaces

steps.label: `show cdp neighbors` there
steps.detail: Find the devices one hop further

visual.loop: Repeat until every device and link is documented

sections.code:
SW2# show cdp neighbors detail
-------------------------
Device ID: SW1
Entry address(es):
  IP address: 1.1.1.1
Platform: cisco WS-C2960XR-24TS-I,  Capabilities: Switch IGMP
Interface: GigabitEthernet1/0/21,  Port ID (outgoing port): GigabitEthernet1/0/24
Holdtime : 144 sec

Version :
Cisco IOS Software, C2960X Software (C2960X-UNIVERSALK9-M), Version 15.2(6)E2, RELEASE SOFTWARE (fc4)

advertisement version: 2
VTP Management Domain: 'fred'

Duplex: full
Management address(es):

! R1 entry omitted
sections.tip: One neighbor fast: show cdp entry NAME. Every neighbor's IP for a mapping exercise: show cdp neighbors detail.
sections.pitfall: Expecting the one-line summary to show IP addresses. It never does; the address is only in the detail or entry output.

check.question: Which piece of information appears in show cdp neighbors detail but not in the one-line show cdp neighbors output?
choices: The neighbor's IP address
The neighbor's hostname
The local interface
The neighbor's port
check.explanation: The summary already shows Device ID, local interface, capability, platform and Port ID. The detail view adds the entry and management addresses, the full software version, native VLAN, duplex and VTP domain.

sections.title: Controlling CDP: timers and on and off
sections.key: CDP is on by default, advertising every 60 seconds with a 180-second holdtime; no cdp run disables it globally and no cdp enable disables one interface.
sections.body:
CDP is enabled by default on Cisco routers and switches, globally and on every interface, and current IOS sends **CDP version 2**.

[[visual]]

The holdtime is a promise to others: your setting tells your **neighbors** how long to keep your entry. When a neighbor goes silent, its entry ages out:

[[visual 2]]

To check CDP itself, use `show cdp` (status and timers), `show cdp interface` (which ports run CDP, with their timers; a `no cdp enable` port is missing) and `show cdp traffic` (version 1 and 2 counters).

[[code]]

visual.title: CDP commands
rows: CDP off or on for the whole device
CDP off or on for that port only
Neighbors keep this device's entry 120 seconds (default 180)

messages.note: Advertisements expected every 60 s never arrive

sections.code:
SW2# show cdp
Global CDP information:
        Sending CDP packets every 60 seconds
        Sending a holdtime value of 180 seconds
        Sending CDPv2 advertisements is enabled

SW2# show cdp traffic
CDP counters :
        Total packets output: 304, Input: 305
! error counters omitted
        CDP version 1 advertisements output: 0, Input: 0
        CDP version 2 advertisements output: 304, Input: 305

SW2# configure terminal
SW2(config)# cdp timer 30
SW2(config)# cdp holdtime 120
SW2(config)# interface gigabitethernet1/0/48
SW2(config-if)# no cdp enable
sections.pitfall: Using no cdp run to hide information from one untrusted port. It also breaks CDP on every trusted link and on phone ports. Use no cdp enable on that interface instead.

check.question: Which command disables CDP on interface Gi0/5 only, leaving it running everywhere else?
choices: no cdp run, in global configuration mode
cdp holdtime 0, in global configuration mode
no lldp transmit, in interface configuration mode
no cdp enable, in interface configuration mode for Gi0/5
check.explanation: no cdp enable works per interface. no cdp run disables CDP on the whole device, and the LLDP command does not affect CDP.

sections.title: CDP as a troubleshooting tool
sections.key: CDP checks cabling against documentation, finds where phones and APs plug in, flags native VLAN and duplex mismatches, and proves Layers 1 and 2 work.
sections.body:
CDP earns its keep in four situations the exam likes to describe:

[[visual]]

[[code]]

Read a mismatch message in order: your interface and its setting first, then the neighbor, its interface and its setting. In the duplex example, SW1 Gi1/0/5 is not full duplex while R3 Gi0/0/0 is.

rows: Docs say SW1 Gi1/0/1 to SW2 Gi1/0/1, but Port ID says Gi1/0/2: the cable landed in the wrong port on SW2
A Cisco phone appears as `SEP` plus its MAC, capabilities H P M, platform IP Phone; APs and switches by hostname and model
CDPv2 compares native VLAN and duplex and logs `%CDP-4-NATIVE_VLAN_MISMATCH` or `%CDP-4-DUPLEX_MISMATCH`
Layers 1 and 2 work: check IP addresses, masks and ACLs
Check the physical layer, interface status and CDP settings first

sections.code:
! Documentation: SW1 Gi1/0/1 <-> SW2 Gi1/0/1
SW1# show cdp neighbors
Device ID        Local Intrfce     Holdtme    Capability  Platform  Port ID
SEP00562B4C1A2F  Gig 1/0/14        151           H P M    IP Phone  Port 1
SW2              Gig 1/0/1         162             S I    WS-C3650  Gig 1/0/2

! Mismatch messages logged by CDP
%CDP-4-NATIVE_VLAN_MISMATCH: Native VLAN mismatch discovered on GigabitEthernet1/0/1 (99), with SW2 GigabitEthernet1/0/2 (1).
%CDP-4-DUPLEX_MISMATCH: duplex mismatch discovered on GigabitEthernet1/0/5 (not full duplex), with R3 GigabitEthernet0/0/0 (full duplex).
sections.pitfall: Disabling CDP to make a mismatch message go away. The message is the symptom; fix the native VLAN or duplex setting on one end instead.

check.question: R1 and R2 cannot ping each other across their direct link, but each lists the other in show cdp neighbors. What does that suggest?
choices: The cable is faulty
Layers 1 and 2 work, so look at IP addressing, masks or ACLs
CDP is disabled on one router
The routers are in different VTP domains
check.explanation: CDP runs directly over the data link, so hearing the neighbor proves the cable, interfaces and Layer 2 are working. A failed ping with working CDP points to a Layer 3 problem such as mismatched subnets or a filtering ACL.

sections.title: LLDP: the open standard
sections.key: LLDP (IEEE 802.1AB) is off by default on Cisco devices: lldp run enables it, and lldp transmit and lldp receive control each direction per interface.
sections.body:
Cisco switches, another vendor's firewall, third-party phones: CDP is not enough. **LLDP** does the same job across vendors, with three differences on Cisco gear:

[[visual]]

So with `lldp run` plus `no lldp receive` on a port, the switch still advertises there but learns no neighbor. Without `lldp run`, `lldp transmit` and `lldp receive` on one port run LLDP on just that port.

[[code]]

Status commands mirror CDP: `show lldp`, `show lldp interface` (Tx and Rx per port) and `show lldp traffic`. If `show lldp neighbors` says `% LLDP is not enabled`, the global `lldp run` is missing.

visual.title: LLDP on Cisco devices
rows: **Disabled**. Enable it for all interfaces with `lldp run` (global)
`lldp transmit` and `lldp receive` (and their `no` forms) control each direction separately and override the global setting either way
Every **30 seconds**, holdtime **120 seconds**, 2-second reinit delay: `lldp timer`, `lldp holdtime`, `lldp reinit`

sections.code:
SW2(config)# lldp run
SW2(config)# interface gigabitethernet1/0/17
SW2(config-if)# no lldp transmit
SW2(config-if)# no lldp receive
SW2(config-if)# interface gigabitethernet1/0/18
SW2(config-if)# no lldp receive
SW2(config-if)# end

SW2# show lldp interface gigabitethernet1/0/18
GigabitEthernet1/0/18:
    Tx: enabled
    Rx: disabled
    Tx state: IDLE
    Rx state: WAIT FOR FRAME
sections.pitfall: Forgetting that LLDP is off by default on Cisco gear. If show lldp neighbors is empty on a Cisco switch, check for lldp run before suspecting the neighbor.

activity.title: Discover your neighbors
activity.prompt: Work through the lab's CDP and LLDP tasks. Remember that LLDP stays off until lldp run, and that per-interface commands (no cdp enable, lldp transmit, lldp receive) override the global ones. After each change, confirm it with show cdp neighbors, show lldp neighbors or show lldp, and before each neighbor command predict which column will hold your own interface.

check.question: A Cisco switch has default settings. A non-Cisco switch connected to it runs only LLDP. What must you do on the Cisco switch to see that neighbor in show lldp neighbors?
choices: Enter lldp run in global configuration mode
Nothing; LLDP is enabled by default
Enter cdp run in global configuration mode
Enter lldp holdtime 120 in global configuration mode
check.explanation: Cisco devices ship with LLDP disabled, so lldp run is required. cdp run affects only CDP, which the other vendor does not speak, and the holdtime is already 120 seconds by default.

sections.title: Reading LLDP neighbor output
sections.key: show lldp neighbors reads like CDP, Local Intf then Port ID, but shows a switch as B and lists only the capabilities a neighbor has enabled.
sections.body:
`show lldp neighbors` has the same **Local Intf** and **Port ID** columns as CDP: local first, neighbor second. What differs:

[[visual]]

`show lldp neighbors detail` and `show lldp entry R1` give the full record, built from **TLVs** (type, length, value):

[[visual 2]]

[[code]]

**LLDP-MED** (Media Endpoint Discovery) adds endpoint TLVs: a network policy that gives a phone its voice VLAN and priority, extended PoE so it can request power, plus inventory and location. It does for third-party phones what CDP does for Cisco phones.

visual.title: LLDP summary versus CDP
rows: B (bridge). S means station, an end host
R router, T telephone, W WLAN AP; no I

visual.title: LLDP TLVs
rows: How long to keep the entry (shown as Time remaining)
What it can do / what it is doing now

sections.code:
SW2# show lldp neighbors
Device ID           Local Intf     Hold-time  Capability      Port ID
R1                  Gi1/0/2        120        R               Gi0/0/1
SW1                 Gi1/0/21       120        B               Gi1/0/24

SW2# show lldp entry R1
Local Intf: Gi1/0/2
Chassis id: 70ea.1a9a.d300
Port id: Gi0/0/1
System Name: R1
System Description:
Cisco IOS Software [Fuji], ISR Software (ARMV8EB_LINUX_IOSD-UNIVERSALK9_IAS-M), Version 16.8.1, RELEASE SOFTWARE (fc3)
Time remaining: 100 seconds
System Capabilities: B,R
Enabled Capabilities: R
Management Addresses:
    IP: 10.12.25.5
! remaining lines omitted
sections.pitfall: Expecting LLDP to show a switch as S. In LLDP, S means station (an end host); a switch shows as B for bridge.

check.question: In show lldp entry R1, System Capabilities shows B,R and Enabled Capabilities shows R. What does that mean?
choices: R1 is bridging and routing right now
R1 is misconfigured
R1 can bridge and route but is currently only routing
R1 supports LLDP on routed ports only
check.explanation: System Capabilities lists what the device supports; Enabled Capabilities lists what its current configuration uses. A difference between the two lines is normal.

sections.title: CDP and LLDP side by side
sections.key: Use LLDP whenever a non-Cisco device is on the link; CDP is Cisco-only but on by default, and the two can run together without conflict.
sections.body:
Exam questions ask which protocol fits and what its defaults are.

[[visual]]

Both run at Layer 2, send to a multicast address that is never forwarded, learn only direct neighbors, and share a family of show commands.

Use **LLDP** with any non-Cisco device: another vendor's switch, a server NIC, a third-party phone. In all-Cisco networks CDP is already on and slightly richer (platform, native VLAN). Many networks run both, each with its own neighbor table.

A neighbor missing from `show cdp neighbors` on a mixed-vendor link? It probably speaks only LLDP, and LLDP is still off on the Cisco side.
sections.tip: LLDP is the newer, faster one: 30 and 120 seconds. CDP is 60 and 180. Each holdtime covers a few missed advertisements.
sections.pitfall: Mixing up the timers. CDP is 60 and 180 seconds; LLDP is 30 and 120 seconds.

check.question: Which pair of default timers belongs to LLDP?
choices: 60-second advertisements, 180-second holdtime
2-second hellos, 20-second max age
30-second advertisements, 120-second holdtime
10-second hellos, 40-second dead interval
check.explanation: LLDP defaults to 30 and 120 seconds, CDP to 60 and 180. The other pairs are STP and OSPF timers.

sections.title: Security: what your switch tells strangers
sections.key: CDP and LLDP hand an attacker your hostname, IP address, model and IOS version, so disable them on untrusted ports but keep them where they do a job.
sections.body:
A laptop on any port sending CDP learns the switch's hostname, management IP, model and exact IOS version: a gift for looking up known vulnerabilities. It can also fake CDP or LLDP-MED messages, pose as a phone, learn the voice VLAN and send tagged frames into it.

[[visual]]

[[code]]

The phone trade-off: turn CDP off where a Cisco IP phone plugs in, and the phone can no longer learn its voice VLAN, so voice lands in the data VLAN or stops working.

visual.title: Where to run discovery
rows: Infrastructure links: switch, router, AP, WLC
Off: `no cdp enable`, `no lldp transmit`, `no lldp receive`
User or guest ports with no phone
Only if nothing relies on it

sections.code:
! Internet-facing router interface: advertise nothing to the ISP
R1(config)# interface gigabitethernet0/0/0
R1(config-if)# description Link to ISP
R1(config-if)# no cdp enable
R1(config-if)# no lldp transmit
R1(config-if)# no lldp receive
sections.deeper: Older IOS releases also had bugs where floods of fake CDP messages could exhaust a device's memory, one more reason to stop listening on ports that face strangers. Tools that craft CDP and LLDP frames are freely available, so treat anything learned on an untrusted port as a claim, not a fact.
sections.pitfall: Disabling CDP everywhere "for security" and then finding every Cisco phone in the data VLAN. Disable discovery where it is risky, not where it does a job.

check.question: Why is leaving CDP enabled on an internet-facing router interface a security concern?
choices: It lets remote users log in without a password
It advertises the router's hostname, IP address, model and IOS version to anyone on that link
It sends the internal routing table to the ISP
It disables the interface's access control lists
check.explanation: CDP shares exactly the details an attacker needs for reconnaissance. It does not grant logins or share routes, but the information leak alone is reason to disable it on untrusted links.

keyTerms.definition: Cisco Discovery Protocol: Cisco-proprietary Layer 2 protocol, enabled by default, that advertises device details to direct neighbors.
Link Layer Discovery Protocol (IEEE 802.1AB): the vendor-neutral equivalent of CDP, disabled by default on Cisco devices.
The neighbor's identifier in CDP and LLDP output, normally its hostname.
The interface on the device where you ran the show command (Local Intrfce or Local Intf).
The neighbor's interface at the far end of the link.
How long a neighbor's entry is kept without a new advertisement: 180 seconds for CDP, 120 for LLDP by default.
Letters describing a neighbor's functions, such as R router and S switch in CDP, or B bridge and T telephone in LLDP.
An LLDP extension for media endpoints that lets non-Cisco phones learn their voice VLAN and power needs.
Interface commands that control sending and processing LLDP messages separately.
Type, length, value: the field format LLDP (and CDP) use to carry each piece of information.
Mandatory LLDP TLV identifying the neighboring device, often by MAC address.
Command that prints the full CDP detail for one named neighbor (show cdp entry SW1).
LLDP lines listing what a neighbor can do and what it is currently doing.
The current CDP version, which adds native VLAN, duplex and VTP domain so switches can detect mismatches.

summary: CDP (Cisco, on by default) and LLDP (IEEE 802.1AB, off by default on Cisco) discover only direct neighbors at Layer 2.
Local Intrfce is your interface; Port ID is the neighbor's.
show cdp neighbors detail and show cdp entry NAME add the IP address, IOS version, native VLAN and duplex.
CDP: 60 and 180 seconds, no cdp run or no cdp enable. LLDP: 30 and 120 seconds, lldp run, lldp transmit, lldp receive.
LLDP shows a switch as B and lists only enabled capabilities; LLDP-MED gives third-party phones their voice VLAN.
Disable discovery on untrusted ports, but keep it on infrastructure links and phone ports.
lesson.feynmanPrompt: Explain to a new engineer how you would use CDP or LLDP to map an unlabeled wiring closet, what each column of show cdp neighbors means, and when you would turn the protocols off.

questions.question: Which statement describes both CDP and LLDP?
choices: Layer 3 protocols that discover every device in the subnet
Routing protocols that exchange neighbor tables
Layer 2 protocols that discover directly connected neighbors
Management protocols that require SSH to run
questions.explanation: Both send advertisements directly in Layer 2 frames to a multicast MAC that is not forwarded, so each device learns only about the devices on the other end of its own links.

questions.question: Match each item to its description.

pairs.right: IEEE 802.1AB, disabled by default on Cisco
Extension that gives third-party phones their voice VLAN

questions.explanation: Knowing the defaults and reading the two interface columns correctly covers most discovery protocol questions.

questions.question: Based on the output, which statement about the link between DSW1 and ASW3 is correct?
questions.code:
DSW1# show cdp neighbors
Capability Codes: R - Router, T - Trans Bridge, B - Source Route Bridge
                  S - Switch, H - Host, I - IGMP, r - Repeater, P - Phone,
                  D - Remote, C - CVTA, M - Two-port Mac Relay

Device ID        Local Intrfce     Holdtme    Capability  Platform  Port ID
ASW3             Gig 1/0/3         170             S I    WS-C2960X Gig 0/1
ASW4             Gig 1/0/4         128             S I    WS-C2960X Gig 0/1
EDGE-R1          Gig 1/0/24        142           R S I    C1111-8P  Gig 0/0/1

Total cdp entries displayed : 3
choices: DSW1 Gi0/1 connects to ASW3 Gi1/0/3
DSW1 Gi1/0/3 connects to ASW3 Gi0/1
Both ends of the link use Gi1/0/3
ASW3 is a router, so it uses Gi0/1
questions.explanation: Local Intrfce (Gig 1/0/3) belongs to DSW1, the device where the command ran, and Port ID (Gig 0/1) belongs to ASW3. ASW3's capabilities S I show a switch, not a router.

questions.question: In this output, how many seconds remain before DSW1 removes EDGE-R1 if no further CDP advertisements arrive?
questions.code:
Device ID        Local Intrfce     Holdtme    Capability  Platform  Port ID
ASW3             Gig 1/0/3         170             S I    WS-C2960X Gig 0/1
EDGE-R1          Gig 1/0/24        142           R S I    C1111-8P  Gig 0/0/1
questions.explanation: Holdtme is the remaining hold time for each entry. It counts down from the neighbor's advertised holdtime (180 by default) and resets whenever a new advertisement arrives.

questions.question: Type the command that shows every CDP neighbor with its IP address, platform and IOS version.
questions.explanation: The detail form adds the entry addresses, full platform, software version, native VLAN and duplex that the one-line summary leaves out.

questions.question: Type the command that shows detailed CDP information for only the neighbor named SW1.
questions.explanation: show cdp entry NAME prints the same detail as show cdp neighbors detail for one neighbor. The name is case sensitive.

questions.question: How often, in seconds, does a Cisco device send CDP advertisements by default?
questions.explanation: CDP advertises every 60 seconds with a 180-second holdtime. LLDP's defaults are 30 and 120.

questions.question: What is CDP's default holdtime in seconds?
questions.explanation: The default CDP holdtime is 180 seconds, three times the 60-second send interval.

questions.question: Type the global configuration command that disables CDP on the entire device.
questions.explanation: no cdp run turns CDP off globally and cdp run turns it back on. To affect one port, use no cdp enable under the interface.

questions.question: In interface configuration mode, type the command that disables CDP on just that interface.
questions.explanation: no cdp enable stops sending and processing CDP on the interface while the rest of the device keeps running CDP.

questions.question: Type the global configuration command that enables LLDP on a Cisco switch.
questions.explanation: LLDP is disabled by default on Cisco devices. lldp run enables it in both directions on interfaces that have no more specific LLDP commands.

questions.question: Given this configuration, which statement about Gi1/0/18 is true?
questions.code:
lldp run
!
interface GigabitEthernet1/0/18
 no lldp receive
choices: The switch learns LLDP neighbors on Gi1/0/18 but does not advertise
LLDP is completely disabled on Gi1/0/18
The global lldp run overrides the interface command, so LLDP runs in both directions
The switch advertises LLDP on Gi1/0/18 but does not learn neighbors from it
questions.explanation: LLDP controls each direction separately and interface commands override lldp run. With no lldp receive, the port still transmits (the default from lldp run) but ignores incoming LLDP, so no neighbor is learned there.

questions.question: What are LLDP's default advertisement interval and holdtime?
choices: 60 seconds and 180 seconds
30 seconds and 120 seconds
30 seconds and 90 seconds
10 seconds and 40 seconds
questions.explanation: LLDP advertises every 30 seconds with a 120-second holdtime. 60 and 180 are CDP's defaults.

questions.question: In show lldp neighbors, a neighboring switch shows capability B. What does B stand for?
choices: Bridge
Backup router
BPDU guard enabled
Broadcast domain
questions.explanation: LLDP uses B (bridge), the older name for the function switches perform. CDP uses S for switch instead.

questions.question: show lldp entry R1 includes these lines. What do they tell you?
questions.code:
System Capabilities: B,R
Enabled Capabilities: R
choices: R1 is currently both bridging and routing
R1 can route and bridge, but only routing is currently enabled
R1 is misconfigured because the two lines differ
R1 accepts LLDP only on routed interfaces
questions.explanation: System Capabilities lists what the device supports; Enabled Capabilities lists what it is using with its current configuration. A difference is normal.

questions.question: Which three statements about CDP are true? (Choose three.)
choices: It is enabled by default on Cisco devices
It is defined in IEEE 802.1AB
It sends advertisements every 60 seconds by default
It can show a neighbor's platform and IOS version
It relays neighbor information to devices two hops away
questions.explanation: CDP is on by default, advertises every 60 seconds and reports platform and version. IEEE 802.1AB defines LLDP, and neither protocol relays advertisements beyond the direct neighbor.

questions.question: A Cisco switch connects to a server whose NIC comes from another vendor. Which protocol should you use so the switch can identify the server's port?
choices: CDP
DTP
LLDP
VTP
questions.explanation: LLDP is the vendor-neutral standard, so non-Cisco devices support it. CDP is Cisco only, and DTP and VTP are not discovery protocols.

questions.question: Why can CDP identify a neighbor even if neither device has an IP address configured?
choices: CDP gets a temporary address from DHCP
CDP relies on ARP to find the neighbor
CDP uses the default gateway to reach the neighbor
CDP runs directly over the data link layer and does not need IP
questions.explanation: CDP messages are carried in Layer 2 frames to a multicast MAC address, with no IP header. That is what makes CDP useful while IP is still broken.

questions.question: SW1 connects to SW2, which connects to R1. From SW1, an engineer needs R1's management IP address. Which approach works?
choices: Run show cdp neighbors detail on SW1; it lists every device in the topology
Run show lldp neighbors on SW1, because LLDP forwards advertisements
Get SW2's IP from show cdp neighbors detail on SW1, SSH to SW2, and run show cdp neighbors detail there
Raise the CDP holdtime so R1's advertisements reach SW1
questions.explanation: Discovery protocols see one hop only, so you walk the network device by device, using each neighbor's IP address from the detail output. Timers do not change how far advertisements travel.

questions.question: Which two interfaces are reasonable places to disable CDP? (Choose two.)
choices: A router interface connected to an ISP
A switch port connected to a Cisco IP phone
A trunk between two distribution switches
A guest access port with no IP phone
An uplink to a Cisco WLC
questions.explanation: Untrusted links (the ISP, guest ports) gain nothing from CDP and leak information. Phone ports need CDP for the voice VLAN, and infrastructure links benefit from it for troubleshooting.

questions.question: After an engineer enters no cdp run on an access switch, the Cisco IP phones start sending voice traffic in the data VLAN. Why?
choices: The phones learned the voice VLAN through CDP, which is now disabled
no cdp run also removes every switchport voice vlan command
DTP stopped negotiating the trunk to each phone
LLDP automatically replaced CDP but advertises VLAN 1
questions.explanation: The switch tells Cisco phones their voice VLAN in CDP. With CDP off, the phones never learn it, so their traffic stays untagged in the data VLAN. The voice VLAN configuration itself is untouched.

questions.question: An engineer configured these timers on SW2. What effect does the holdtime setting have?
questions.code:
SW2# show cdp
Global CDP information:
        Sending CDP packets every 30 seconds
        Sending a holdtime value of 120 seconds
        Sending CDPv2 advertisements is enabled
choices: SW2 keeps its neighbors' entries for 120 seconds
SW2 sends an advertisement every 120 seconds
SW2's neighbors keep SW2's entry for up to 120 seconds after the last advertisement
Neighbors must use the same holdtime or CDP fails
questions.explanation: The holdtime travels inside SW2's advertisements and tells receivers how long to keep SW2's information. SW2's own neighbor table follows the holdtimes its neighbors advertise. CDP timers do not have to match.

questions.question: In show cdp neighbors, what does the Device ID column normally contain?
choices: The neighbor's MAC address
The neighbor's hostname
The local switch's serial number
The VLAN the neighbor belongs to
questions.explanation: Device ID is the identifier the neighbor advertises, normally its configured hostname.

questions.question: SW2 is powered off. Put the events on SW1 in order, assuming default CDP timers.
items: SW1 receives SW2's last advertisement, which carries a holdtime of 180 seconds
SW1's Holdtme counter for SW2 starts counting down
SW2 loses power and stops advertising
The advertisements expected every 60 seconds never arrive
The counter reaches zero and SW1 removes SW2 from its neighbor table
questions.explanation: Each advertisement resets the countdown. When three 60-second intervals pass with nothing received, the 180-second holdtime runs out and the entry is deleted.

questions.question: Why do security guides recommend disabling CDP and LLDP on untrusted ports?
questions.answer: Because they advertise the device's hostname, management IP address, model and software version to anyone on the link, which helps an attacker plan an attack. Keep them only where they do a job, such as infrastructure links and phone ports.
questions.explanation: Discovery protocols trade convenience for information exposure, so the decision is made per port.

questions.question: An engineer entered these commands on a Cisco switch to see a third-party neighbor, but show lldp neighbors returns '% LLDP is not enabled'. What is missing?
questions.code:
SW1(config)# lldp timer 30
SW1(config)# lldp holdtime 120
SW1(config)# interface gigabitethernet0/1
SW1(config-if)# description To vendor-X switch
SW1(config-if)# end
SW1# show lldp neighbors
% LLDP is not enabled
choices: The holdtime must be 180 seconds
CDP must be disabled before LLDP can run
The global lldp run command
lldp timer must be set under the interface
questions.explanation: Setting LLDP timers does not turn LLDP on. Cisco devices have LLDP disabled until lldp run is configured. CDP and LLDP can run together.

questions.question: Both commands were run on SW2. Why does R1 show R S I in one output but only R in the other?
questions.code:
SW2# show cdp neighbors | include R1
R1               Gig 1/0/2         131           R S I    C1111-8P  Gig 0/0/1

SW2# show lldp neighbors | include R1
R1                  Gi1/0/2        120        R               Gi0/0/1
choices: LLDP shows only the first capability letter to save space
CDP lists all supported capabilities, while LLDP lists only the enabled ones
R1 stopped switching between the two commands
LLDP does not support routers with switch ports
questions.explanation: CDP lists every capability the neighbor supports, while the LLDP summary lists the capabilities the neighbor has enabled. R1 can switch and do IGMP but is only routing. LLDP also has no IGMP code at all.

questions.question: SW1 logs this message. What does it tell you?
questions.code: %CDP-4-DUPLEX_MISMATCH: duplex mismatch discovered on GigabitEthernet1/0/5 (not full duplex), with R3 GigabitEthernet0/0/0 (full duplex).
choices: R3 has CDP disabled on Gi0/0/0
The native VLANs on the link differ
SW1 Gi1/0/5 is not in full duplex while R3 Gi0/0/0 is, so the link has a duplex mismatch
The cable between SW1 and R3 is a crossover cable
questions.explanation: CDP version 2 advertises the sending port's duplex. SW1's Gi1/0/5 is not running full duplex while R3's Gi0/0/0 is, a duplex mismatch that causes late collisions and poor performance. Fix the duplex (usually by letting both ends autonegotiate or setting both the same).

questions.question: Type the command that shows the full LLDP details (chassis ID, system name, description, capabilities and management address) for every LLDP neighbor.
questions.explanation: show lldp neighbors detail prints the full TLV contents for every neighbor; show lldp entry NAME does the same for one neighbor.

questions.question: From this output on SW2, what IP address would you SSH to in order to manage SW1?
questions.code:
SW2# show cdp entry SW1
-------------------------
Device ID: SW1
Entry address(es):
  IP address: 1.1.1.1
Platform: cisco WS-C2960XR-24TS-I,  Capabilities: Switch IGMP
Interface: GigabitEthernet1/0/21,  Port ID (outgoing port): GigabitEthernet1/0/24
Holdtime : 144 sec
! version omitted
Management address(es):
  IP address: 1.1.1.1
questions.explanation: The Entry address and Management address lines both list 1.1.1.1, SW1's advertised management address. Gi1/0/24 is SW1's port, not an address.

questions.question: Which three items does show cdp neighbors detail add that the one-line show cdp neighbors output does not show? (Choose three.)
choices: The neighbor's IP address
The neighbor's IOS version
The Device ID
The native VLAN of the neighbor's port
The local interface
questions.explanation: The detail view adds addresses, the full software version, and version 2 extras such as native VLAN, duplex and VTP domain. The Device ID and the local interface are already in the summary.

questions.question: Match each LLDP field to what it contains.

pairs.right: Identifier of the neighboring device, often a MAC address
The neighbor's interface on this link
Seconds until the entry ages out
Functions the neighbor is using now

questions.explanation: Chassis ID and Port ID identify the neighbor and its port, Time remaining counts down from the advertised holdtime, and the two capability lines separate what the device can do from what it is doing.

questions.question: Type the command that lists the interfaces running CDP along with their send and holdtime timers.
questions.explanation: show cdp interface shows CDP status per interface. An interface configured with no cdp enable does not appear in the list.

questions.question: In show cdp neighbors on an access switch, a neighbor appears with Device ID SEP00562B4C1A2F, capabilities H P M and platform IP Phone. What is it?
choices: A Cisco IP phone
A wireless access point
A router running IGMP
A misconfigured switch
questions.explanation: Cisco IP phones advertise a Device ID of SEP plus their MAC address and the phone capability P. The H P M codes mean host, phone and two-port MAC relay (the phone's built-in switch).

questions.question: Which IEEE standard defines LLDP? (For example, 802.1Q.)
questions.explanation: LLDP is IEEE 802.1AB. 802.1Q defines VLAN tagging and 802.3ad defines link aggregation (LACP).

questions.question: You can reach only SW1 and must document the network behind it with CDP. Put the steps in order.
items: Run show cdp neighbors on SW1 and note each neighbor and both interfaces
Run show cdp neighbors detail to get each neighbor's IP address
SSH to the first neighbor using that address
Run show cdp neighbors on that neighbor to find the devices one hop further
Repeat until every device and link is documented
questions.explanation: CDP sees one hop, so mapping is a loop: list neighbors, get each one's address from the detail output, log in to it and repeat, recording links as you go.

questions.question: The documentation says SW1 Gi1/0/1 connects to SW2 Gi1/0/1, and SW2 Gi1/0/1 has the trunk configuration. Based on the output from SW1, what is the problem?
questions.code:
SW1# show cdp neighbors gigabitethernet1/0/1
Device ID        Local Intrfce     Holdtme    Capability  Platform  Port ID
SW2              Gig 1/0/1         162             S I    WS-C3650  Gig 1/0/2
choices: SW1 is using the wrong local port
The cable lands on SW2 Gi1/0/2 instead of Gi1/0/1
CDP is disabled on SW2 Gi1/0/1
SW2 is a router, not a switch
questions.explanation: Port ID is SW2's interface, so the cable lands on SW2 Gi1/0/2, not Gi1/0/1. The trunk configuration sits on the wrong SW2 port. Re-cable or move the configuration.

questions.question: Which three TLVs must be present in every LLDP message? (Choose three.)
choices: Chassis ID
System Name
Port ID
Management Address
Time to Live
questions.explanation: Every LLDPDU carries Chassis ID, Port ID and Time to Live (and ends with an End of LLDPDU marker). System name, management address and the capability TLVs are optional, though Cisco devices send them by default.

questions.question: A company replaces its Cisco phones with another vendor's phones. What lets the new phones learn their voice VLAN and request PoE power from the Cisco switches?
choices: DTP on the phone ports
VTP client mode on the phones
CDP version 2
LLDP-MED
questions.explanation: LLDP-MED adds network policy (voice VLAN and markings), extended power, inventory and location TLVs for media endpoints. CDP is Cisco only, and DTP and VTP do not talk to phones.

questions.question: The goal was to stop discovery protocols only on Gi0/0/0, the link to the ISP, and keep them on internal links. What is wrong with this configuration?
questions.code:
R1(config)# no cdp run
R1(config)# lldp run
R1(config)# interface gigabitethernet0/0/0
R1(config-if)# description Link to ISP
R1(config-if)# no lldp transmit
R1(config-if)# no lldp receive
choices: no lldp receive must be entered before no lldp transmit
lldp run re-enables LLDP on Gi0/0/0 and overrides the interface commands
no cdp run disables CDP on every interface; no cdp enable under Gi0/0/0 was needed
The description must say "untrusted" for the commands to apply
questions.explanation: no cdp run is global, so CDP stops on every interface, including internal links and phone-facing ports. The interface command no cdp enable under Gi0/0/0 was what the goal needed. The LLDP lines are correctly scoped to the ISP interface.
